title: Marc Lawrence Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Marc Lawrence Playbook review, checked 20 Nov 2026: real prices, pay after you win, his report card recounted, and a forum tracker's newsletter records.
dek: A long running football newsletter and pick business. Single picks cost $40 to $60 on a pay after you win basis, newsletters run $11 an issue to $65 a season, and pick specials run $99 to $199. The seller grades its own report card, and its headline records did not match our count. An independent forum tracker that grades the newsletter plays at the printed lines shows 2025 NFL star plays at 26-27-1.

short_answer: Playbook Sports is a real, long running business. It names an operating company, posts phone lines with hours, publishes prices for every product, and sells a printed football magazine and weekly newsletters that bettors on forums have discussed for twenty years. In that sense it is legitimate.

Whether Marc Lawrence's picks make money is a separate question. His own report card showed 43 wins, 26 losses and 1 push over 90 days on 20 Nov 2026, but it lists only package names such as "Never Lost 100% ATS NFL Perfect System Club Play!" with a W or L, and no team, line, odds or profit. The headline records on his sales pages did not match the totals we counted from it. Plays sold on a "100%", "Never Lost" or perfect angle went 23-19-1 on that same report card.

The best outside evidence is a TheRX member who grades the Playbook newsletter plays every week at the printed lines. That tracker had his 2025 NFL 5 star plays at 7-11 and all NFL star plays at 26-27-1, and his 2026 college 5 star plays at 9-1 through 9 Nov. Pay after you win on single picks is the most buyer friendly part, but it never covers what you lose on the bets. Start with single picks or one newsletter issue and keep your own record.

guarantee: Playbook sells its single guaranteed picks two ways. With Pay After You Win, the Picks Policy, read again on 20 Nov 2026, says "your card isn't charged until the game finishes and you show a net profit." It adds: "If the purchase nets more units won than lost, your card is charged the next day. Anything less than a net profit, and you're not charged at all." Profit is counted at $100 per star, and the package price counts against you: the page's own example says a $35 package with one 5 star winner and two 3 star losers nets minus $195, so you owe nothing. If you pay with Playbook's own Playbucks tokens instead, "you receive an equal amount back as replacement Tokens", not cash.

The second way, Discount Pre Paid, gives "an automatic 20% discount off the Pay After You Win price". The policy states "there is no refund on pre-paid purchases" and that "all losing purchases are returned in full as Reusable Makeup Tokens". It also says "the Best in the Business Guarantee™ does NOT apply to those subscriptions", meaning prepaid weekly or monthly packages. The $99 weekend and $199 November specials carry no guarantee wording on their product pages.

One wording problem: the Today's Picks page still says "Our guaranteed picks come with a full money-back promise" and then "If the pick doesn't win, you get a free pick in return." Those are not the same thing. Read the Picks Policy, which is the detailed version. No option covers the money you lose on the bets themselves.

claims_note: We recounted Marc's 90 day report card on 20 Nov 2026. It lists 70 plays from 22 Aug to 15 Nov 2026: 43 wins, 26 losses and 1 push, which is the 62.32% shown once pushes are left out. Football plays from the NFL opener on 10 Sep through 15 Nov went 36-20-1 (64.3%). The run has cooled: plays from 27 Oct to 15 Nov went 7-8, and the last 30 days stood at 11-10 (52.38%). None of this shows odds or units, so none of it can be turned into profit.

The sales headlines still do not match. The November Special page, live on 20 Nov 2026, says "29-9" from the start of the NFL season through 26 Oct; the report card entries for 10 Sep to 26 Oct add up to 29-12-1. On 7 Nov the profile claimed 31-12; the same entries added up to 31-15-1. Playbook may count differently, for example by leaving out some plays, but none of the pages we read says how. One claim does roughly check out: the Game of the Year blurb says he is 10-1 on featured top plays this season, and plays with "Top" in their title went 11-1 on the report card.

Pick names do much of the selling. Plays are titled with historical angles such as "27-1 ATS", "16-0 ATS" or "Never Lost 100% ATS". Those numbers describe past games that fit a pattern, not Marc's record. On the 90 day report card, plays named for a 100%, never lost, perfect system or X-0 angle went 23-19-1 (54.8%), while his other plays went 20-7. An angle found by searching decades of games for a perfect subset says little about the next game.
The experience figures shift by page: 1975 on the profile, Est. 1984 on the homepage, "Over 40 years" in the banner. None of that is proof of results either way.
record: What is independently verifiable: no full, time stamped log of Marc's paid picks kept by a third party, no contest standings we could open, and no court or regulator record involving Marc Lawrence or Playbook in our searches. A forum member said Marc placed 7th in the Westgate SuperContest a few years ago, but we could not find the standings to confirm it.

The closest thing to an outside record covers the newsletter, not the paid phone plays. A TheRX member posts weekly "Newsletter Tracking" that grades the rated plays "at the lines listed in the newsletters at the time the plays were published." For the 2025 season (through 25 Jan 2026) that tracker had Playbook NFL 5 star plays at 7-11, 4 star at 9-9 and 3 star at 10-7-1, so 26-27-1 on all NFL star plays, and college 5, 4 and 3 star plays at 21-23-1. The Awesome Angle feature was the bright spot at 17-6-1. For 2026 through 9 Nov the tracker had college 5 star plays at 9-1, 4 star 7-3 and 3 star 3-7 (19-11 in all), and NFL star plays at 14-13. These are one forum member's counts that we did not regrade, but they use a clear method and include losing categories.

What is the seller's own marketing: Playbook grades its own experts on an Experts Report Card. Each entry shows only the date, the package title and W, L or T. There is no team, side, line, odds, star rating or units won, so a buyer cannot tell whether those wins made money at the prices they could get.

What buyers say about the paid plays: in October 2025 a long time TheRX member posted his own tally of Marc's late phone plays for that football season at 24-42, down more than 70 units, and another member listed 11 straight losing paid plays from 19 to 27 Oct 2025. Neither posted a full log we could check, but both are consistent with the tracker's weak 2025 NFL newsletter numbers.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Marc Lawrence or Playbook Sports pick is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Marc Lawrence or the Playbook experts perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Playbook's own report card put Marc at 62% over 90 days, while a forum tracker had his 2025 NFL newsletter star plays at 26-27-1. On the Watchdog board on 20 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent evidence on Playbook Sports is mostly forum talk, plus one forum member's weekly grading of the newsletter plays. We found no review site sample we could count. Comments split between readers who value the magazine and data and bettors who doubt the paid picks.

customers.text: We found about twenty independent posts on Marc Lawrence and Playbook across TheRX (2005 to 2026), Sportsbook Review (2007 to 2014) and Covers (2021 and 2023), plus a weekly newsletter tracker on TheRX. The pattern is steady over two decades: bettors respect the Playbook as reading material and doubt the paid picks. Readers in 2010, 2014, 2021 and 2025 called the magazine and newsletters useful research, and several said he does not chase losses or push all in bets. On the other side, Covers members in 2023 called his stacked trends data mining, Sportsbook Review members in 2007 and 2008 said his playbook picks hit about 40 percent one year and that his monitored record was poor, a 2005 TheRX customer of ten years said a bad season cost them heavily, and in October 2025 TheRX members posted a 24-42 tally and an 11 game losing streak on his paid phone plays. The tracker's numbers fit that split: the 2025 NFL newsletter star plays were about even, while the college 5 star plays started 2026 at 9-1. A few members made personal allegations about his name or sales tactics with no evidence; we do not repeat them as fact.

In TheRX newsletters thread, a member posted their own tally of Marc's paid late phone plays for the 2025 football season: 0-4 on 5 star, 6-7 on 4 star and 17-29 on 3 star, 24-42 overall with some 2 unit plays, down more than 70 units. Another member listed 11 straight losing paid plays from 19 to 27 Oct 2025, and others said the newsletter had done better than the paid plays that year. A member added that his top plays had historically done well but that it was a bad year. No full log was posted, and the tier figures as posted add to 23-40.

A TheRX member who grades newsletter plays each week at the printed lines posted final 2025 season numbers for the Playbook: NFL 5 star 7-11, 4 star 9-9, 3 star 10-7-1; college 5 star 6-8-1, 4 star 7-8, 3 star 8-7; and the Awesome Angle feature 17-6-1, which they listed among the season's best records. The same thread showed members doubting a Playbook claim about a Super Bowl angle.

The same tracker's update through 9 Nov 2026 had the Playbook's college 5 star plays at 9-1, 4 star 7-3, 3 star 3-7, the upset pick 7-3 and the Awesome Angle 9-3. NFL star plays were 5-4, 5-4 and 4-5. Another member noted the college 5 star record in the thread. These are newsletter plays at printed lines, not the paid phone plays.

Earlier in TheRX newsletters thread, a long time member wrote that Marc claimed 9-1 on 4 and 5 star NFL picks over five weeks, and posted their own tally of 4-3 on 5 star and 5-2 on 4 star NFL picks for that season. Other members replied that the member was mixing up the newsletter picks with the paid phone service picks, and one said Marc had not lied. We did not verify either tally.
In a TheRX thread about football services, a member dismissed Marc's picks and claimed he does not bet his own games. No evidence was posted.

In reply, another member called Marc's magazine and newsletter "essential reading" for study, said he had placed 7th in the Westgate SuperContest a few years earlier, and added that nobody hits more than about 57% long term. They praised the research, not the paid picks. We could not confirm the contest finish.

In a Covers thread on the Playbook, one member wondered whether Marc picks games first and then finds trends to justify them, and another said his picks show no understanding of data mining, because adding more conditions to a trend search makes the result more random and less predictive.
A Covers member shared a sale link for the Playbook magazine and said readers could sample pages from the previous year's edition. It is a pointer to the magazine, not a report of results.

In a Sportsbook Review thread, a member who saw Marc on a cable fantasy sports network asked whether he could be trusted. Replies were split: one called him a roughly even capper, another said his weekly newsletter is worth reading, and a member who said they had followed him for at least 15 years called the database useful and said he does not chase losses or use all in bets. Others said trend based picks are mostly useless and that they would not pay for them.

In an older Sportsbook Review thread, a member who subscribed to the newsletter for two seasons said they still buy the Playbook magazine for its technical data, and another called the newsletters useful tools but said following week old picks blindly will not profit. Others said similar information is free online or that midweek newsletters are old news by the time they arrive.

In a Sportsbook Review thread about another handicapper, one member said in January 2007 that Marc's playbook picks had hit about 40 percent the year before, while others said his free write ups were a good read even in a tough year but not worth paying for. In May 2008 a member said Marc's record was independently monitored, unlike some rivals, so it was credible, though poor at the time. Neither posted a log.

On TheRX, a member who said they had been Marc's customer for ten years said that season had been bad and cost them heavily, but that three winning 10 star game of the year plays at the end won some of it back. In the same thread other members said picks sellers know little more than their buyers and called him a good marketer, with no evidence.

We found no Reddit thread with a real discussion of Playbook's paid picks (one 2025 r/sportsbetting post only mentioned the magazine as a model when asking for an NHL equivalent), no Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm belongs to playbooksports.com, and no app store listing. Trustpilot blocked our earlier check. We saw no customer testimonials on the Playbook pages we read.

conflicts: Playbook's roster sells picks from other services under its own roof, including Doc's Sports and Jim Feist, and the free pick of the day on 7 Nov 2026 was a Doc's Sports play ending with a pitch for Doc's packages. A buyer should know that Playbook earns from selling other handicappers' picks, not just Marc's.

The daily Coffee Club e-letter on 7 Nov 2026 quoted election odds from "three of the leading offshore sportsbooks," naming Bovada and BetOnline. We did not see sportsbook signup links, promo codes or revenue share links on the Playbook pages we read. Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators.
In September 2024 the football depth chart site Ourlads announced a partnership to feature Playbook and its pay after you win picks. That page is promotional and is not an independent review.
The weekly newsletter tracking we cite is posted in a forum thread where members also share copies of paid newsletters. We use only the tracker's graded totals.
strengths: A named operating company, posted phone lines with hours and a full price list for every product.
Pay after you win on single guaranteed picks: you are billed only if the purchase shows a net profit, with a worked example on the policy page.
Low cost ways to sample: single newsletter issues from $11, a $20 PDF preview guide, a free daily e-letter and a weekly podcast.
A daily report card that does show recent losses, including the 7-8 stretch from late October to mid November 2026, rather than only hot runs.

His newsletter plays are graded by an outside forum tracker each week at the printed lines, and some features, such as the Awesome Angle (17-6-1 in 2025) and the 2026 college 5 star plays (9-1), have done well there.
concerns: The report card shows W or L by package name only. No line, odds, star rating or units, so profit cannot be checked.
Headline records (29-9, 31-12) did not match our count from the seller's own report card, and the 29-9 claim was still on sale on 20 Nov 2026.
Plays sold on "100%", "Never Lost" and perfect system angles went only 23-19-1 on the seller's own 90 day report card.
The outside tracker had his 2025 NFL newsletter star plays at 26-27-1, and forum members reported a 24-42 run and 11 straight losses on paid plays in October 2025.
No guarantee on prepaid subscriptions, no stated loss terms on the $99 and $199 specials, and prepaid losses come back as tokens, not cash.
Prices for the same product moved sharply within two weeks, such as the November Special going from $349 to $199.
checklist: Ask for every paid pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds, the star rating and the time it was sent. A report card of package names is not a record.
Prefer Pay After You Win over Discount Pre Paid unless you are sure you want makeup tokens instead of cash back.
Read the play name as an advert. A "100% ATS" angle is about past games, not about Marc's results.
If you buy for research, try one newsletter issue ($11 to $15) before a season, and compare its rated plays with the forum tracker's totals.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Playbook Sports is a real business run by Playbook Enterprises Inc., with phone lines, published prices and decades of football publications. We could not verify that Marc's paid picks win over time, because his only record is a report card the seller grades itself, without lines or odds.
How much does Marc Lawrence cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 Marc's single guaranteed picks were $40 or $60 pay after you win, with prepaid 20% cheaper. His weekend special was $99 and his November special $199; his 7 day and 30 day packages were $149 and $399 when last shown on 7 Nov. Playbook newsletters ran from $11 an issue to $65 for the rest of the season, and VIP membership from $69 a month.
Does Marc Lawrence have a verified record?

No. Playbook's own report card showed 43 wins, 26 losses and 1 push over 90 days on 20 Nov 2026, but it lists only package names and results, with no line, odds or units. The only outside grading we found covers the newsletter, where a TheRX member had his 2025 NFL star plays at 26-27-1.
How does Pay After You Win work?

Your card is authorised but charged only if the purchase shows a net profit, counted at $100 per star with the price counted against you. If you prepay for the 20% discount, losses come back as reusable tokens, not cash, and the guarantee does not cover weekly or monthly subscriptions.
Are the Playbook newsletters better than the paid picks?

Forum members often say so, and in October 2025 several said the newsletter was beating the paid plays. The outside tracker's numbers are mixed: weak 2025 NFL star plays, a strong 2025 Awesome Angle and strong 2026 college 5 star plays.

For the money you get football picks built on historical betting angles, or newsletters and a yearly magazine that many forum bettors value as research. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays at the lines a buyer can get; pay after you win limits what you pay for losing single picks but not what you lose betting them.
